_comment: `sql` is the exact rendered predicate. Params are asserted alongside the statement text so
that a value being interpolated into the SQL string instead of bound as a parameter shows up
`mustFailClosed: true` marks an input for which the translator must NOT produce a filter that
leaves rows visible. Accepted outcomes: a thrown error, or a never-true predicate (1=0 /
false). Rewritten in JR-13-01 (epic E13): until 2026-07-28 these three entries carried
`failOpen: true` plus `sql: null` and thereby asserted the defect (F3) as if it were the
contract. `observedBeforeE13` records what the helper did then, so the change of expectation
is legible. These cases are RED until JR-13-04 lands.

cases.name: known relation key becomes qualified column
unknown relation key must fail closed
cases.note: INVERTED in JR-13-06 (finding F21, decided by the PO 2026-07-29: strict allowlist). This case used to pin the emitted identifier. There is no column literally named foo.bar, so the old behaviour made every FilterBuilder-scoped query fail at runtime instead of denying access; an unresolvable relation is a policy error and is refused. Marked `mustRefuseKey` and not `mustFailClosed` so that the count of F3 cases stays what JR-13-01 set it to.

cases.name: $in with an empty list is fail-closed
literal null becomes = NULL, not IS NULL
cases.note: Never matches any row. Fail-closed, but silently: $exists is the working form.

cases.name: empty query must fail closed
cases.note: JR-13-01/F3: an empty condition object carries no restriction, so translating it to "no filter" hands the caller an unscoped query. FilterBuilder already special-cases the empty query to 1=0; the translator must not be the one place where it means "everything".

cases.name: unsupported operator must fail closed
cases.note: JR-13-01/F3: the switch has no default branch, so an unknown operator is dropped and the condition disappears entirely. Required behaviour (JR-13-04): reject, or emit a never-true predicate.

cases.name: empty $or must fail closed
cases.note: JR-13-01/F3: an empty disjunction satisfies nothing, so it must not translate to "no filter".

cases.name: second operator in the same object is dropped
cases.note: Only Object.keys(value)[0] is read. The $lte bound is silently lost.
